messages.content: use meets about my brother and a friend.
my brother meets a friend after work.
now make it yesterday.
my brother met a friend after work yesterday.
can i use meet with they?
yes. they meet after work.
now ask if he met the friend.
did my brother meet the friend after work?
why meet after did?
did goes with meet in that question. met works without did in the sentence about yesterday.
can you know they had a plan to meet?
not from meet or met alone. they might have chosen it before, or seen each other without a plan.
make that answer shorter.
the sentence does not say whether they chose a time before seeing each other.
only give the first brother sentence again.
my brother meets a friend after work.
write a longer story using waits and meets about two people who have the same time but different places in mind. let a message help them find each other.

a woman waits near the library door to meet her brother. he waits by the park because they had talked about walking there after the visit. both have the same time in mind, but they have kept different places from the conversation. after a few minutes, she sends a short message asking where he is waiting. he answers that he is by the park, and she says she is at the library door. they look at the plan again and choose one place clearly. he comes to the door, where she meets him with the book she wanted to show. neither needs to choose a feeling from the waiting time. a question about place gives the information they need, and they still have time for the walk.
what detail did they have the same?
the meeting time.
what detail was different?
the place where each waited.
make the important idea of that story more simple.
they asked where the other person was and found they were waiting in different places.
write her first message.
where are you waiting? i am near the library door.
finish with them walking together.
he comes to the door, she puts the book away, and they walk to the park side by side.
is my sister plays a game right?
yes. my sister plays a game is a full sentence.
now use we.
we play a game.
make it yesterday.
we played a game yesterday.
now ask if she did it yesterday.
did my sister play a game yesterday?
why play after did?
did goes with play in that question. plays goes with my sister when telling what she does, and played can tell about yesterday.
can you know how the game finished?
no. you only said she played it, not how it finished.
make that answer shorter.
no. playing does not say how it finished.
only give the first sister sentence again.
my sister plays a game.
i drew a face today and spent more time on one eye than on the rest.
what made that part need more time for you?
i liked the way the eye looked, and i wanted the other one to look like it.
you wanted the two eyes to look similar.
make that reply shorter.
you wanted them to look similar.
can you help me say that without saying every face has to look the same?
i wanted the eyes in this drawing to look similar to each other.
what if i leave them different because i like it?
then that can be your choice for the picture. the goal is what you want this drawing to show, not a rule for every face.
now add a simple line about the nose and ears without choosing their shape.
i also drew the nose and ears.
can you know the drawing is of me?
no. you have not said who it is a picture of.
only give my sentence about the eyes again.
i wanted the eyes in this drawing to look similar to each other.
give a sentence with speaks about my teacher.
my teacher speaks slowly.
now make it about yesterday.
my teacher spoke slowly yesterday.
can speaks go with they?
use speak with they: they speak slowly.
what if i ask the teacher to do it?
could you speak slowly, please?
why speak after could you?
that request has speak. speaks is used with my teacher or she in the sentence about what the person does.
can slowly mean the words are easy?
not by itself. someone can speak slowly and still use hard words.
make that explanation shorter.
someone can speak slowly and still use hard words.
only give the request again.
could you speak slowly, please?
write a longer story about someone asking a person to speak slowly and then learning they also need simple words. keep both people kind.

a child listens while his aunt reads a story. she speaks slowly, but some words are new to him. at first, he asks her to slow down again. she does, but the meaning is still not clear. then she asks which part is hard. he gives her the sentence and says he does not know a word in it. she gives a simple sentence with the same idea, then gives the meaning of the new word. he can follow the story after that. a slow voice had given him time, but time alone had not given the word meaning. before the next story, he asks for simple words and says he will ask when a word is new. she does not need to choose a meaning for his quiet without asking.
why did the slow voice not answer the whole problem?
he did not know one of the words, so more time alone did not explain it.
what helped after that?
she gave a simple sentence and explained the new word.
make the important idea in that story more simple.
she used words he knew, then helped him learn the new word too.
write the child request.
could you use simple words and help me when a word is new?
finish with him asking at the right part.
when another new word comes, he stops her and asks about that word. she answers, and they go on with the story.
is my father watches a film a full sentence?
yes. it says what your father does, or can be part of a story about now.
now use i.
i watch a film.
now make it yesterday.
i watched a film yesterday.
make it about my father yesterday.
my father watched a film yesterday.
ask if he did that.
did my father watch a film yesterday?
can you know he liked it?
no. watching a film does not by itself tell us whether he liked it.
use words without watching.
seeing the film and having a good feeling about it are different things.
only give the first father sentence again.
my father watches a film.
in my drawing, there are two arms and two legs. how many of those parts did i draw?
four parts.
can you know it is a drawing of a real person?
not from those details alone. you have not said whether it is real or made up.
now i add one eye, a nose, and two ears.
then you have added four more parts from that list.
how many parts did i give in all?
eight: two arms, two legs, one eye, one nose, and two ears.
make that answer shorter.
there are eight parts in the details you gave.
can you know whether i want another eye in the picture?
no. you would need to say what you want to draw.
only give the number of ears i gave.
two ears.
write a longer story about a child being asked to look at the bottom of a page, but looking at the bottom of the book instead. make the request more clear through a question.

a child holds a book while his sister talks about a picture. she asks him to look at the bottom. he moves the whole book to look at the outside. she stops and asks what he thinks bottom is about. he says he thought she wanted the bottom of the book. she had wanted the bottom of the page they were reading. they open it again, and she puts her hand near the line below the picture. next time, she says bottom of this page instead of using only bottom. the place word had not been wrong, but it needed the thing it was about. after that, the child can follow her explanation without turning the book away from the picture.
what did he look at first?
the bottom of the whole book.
what did she want him to look at?
the bottom of the page they were reading.
make the important idea in the story more simple.
she makes the place clear by saying which page and putting her hand near the line.
make that answer shorter.
she says which page and which part.
finish with the book open to the picture.
he holds the book open, and they read the line under the picture together.
my friend made soup. i like it, but i do not know what is in it. give me a question without choosing the vegetables myself.
what did you put in the soup?
can i ask about cream if i think there is some?
yes, as a question rather than a fact: is there cream in the soup?
make that answer shorter.
yes. ask whether it is there instead of saying you know.
what if they say no, it is milk?
then use that answer instead of keeping cream as a fact.
write a short thank you for telling me.
thank you for telling me. i liked the soup.
only give the thank you again.
thank you for telling me. i liked the soup.
can you know whether it had butter too?
no. you have not given that detail.
what is the difference between push and pull?
push can move something away from you. pull can bring it to you.
make that explanation shorter.
push away from you. pull to you.
if i see a closed door, can i know which it needs?
not from being closed alone. you would need to know how the door works.
can you write two simple sentences asking for those things?
please push the container away from the table. please pull the chair to the table.
why not tell me to push every door?
because a door being closed does not tell us how it opens. you need to know that before choosing what to do.
make that answer shorter.
being closed does not say how the door opens.
only give the chair request again.
please pull the chair to the table.
write a longer story about someone asking the price of an object the person does not want to sell. keep it about a chair and make the conversation kind.

a woman builds chairs in a small room near her house. a person visiting sees a pink chair near the door and asks how much it is. the woman says that this chair is for her own kitchen and is not one she wants to sell. the person says sorry and asks whether she makes other chairs to sell. she says yes and gives a page with examples. the first question had been about buying, but not every chair in the room was something to buy. they talk about the kind of chair the person wants, and she asks about size and color before giving a price. asking about money had started the conversation, but knowing the use was needed before choosing the object.
why did the woman not give a price for the pink chair?
it was for her own kitchen, not something she wanted to sell.
what did the person ask next?
whether she made other chairs to sell.
make the important difference in the story more simple.
the pink chair was for the woman herself. she made other chairs that people could buy.
why ask about size and color before a price?
she needed to know what kind of chair the person wanted.
finish with the question about the kitchen use.
she asked how much space there was by the table, and the person began telling her about the room.
use cuts in a sentence about a person and paper.
my sister cuts the paper.
now use they instead.
they cut the paper.
now ask my sister to do it.
could you cut the paper, please?
why cut after could you?
the request has cut. cuts goes with my sister or she in the sentence about what happens.
what if i use yesterday with cut?
my sister cut the paper yesterday.
does cut always look different in the past?
no. cut can be the same written word for now and before, with context giving the time.
only give the first sister sentence again.
my sister cuts the paper.
i can receive a message and still not know my answer right away.
yes. reading the question and having the answer ready are different parts.
help me tell someone that in a kind way.
i have seen your message. i need a little time before answering.
can i add that i did see the message?
yes. i have seen your message makes that clear. you can say that and ask for a little time.
just make the message shorter.
i saw your message and need a little time to answer.
why not say yes before i have had time to think?
because answering before you know can give the wrong idea. you can say you need time.
make that answer shorter.
you can say you need time instead of giving a yes you have not chosen.
only give the short message again.
i saw your message and need a little time to answer.
use however in two sentences about a book i like that is also hard.
i like the book. however, some sentences are hard for me.
can both parts be true?
yes. you can like the book and find some parts hard at the same time.
why use however?
it helps show that you like the book without saying every part is easy.
make that explanation shorter.
it makes clear that the book is not easy in every part.
now make it about a drawing.
i like the drawing. however, i want to change one part.
does that mean i hate the whole picture?
no. you can like the picture and still want one part different.
make that answer shorter.
one part can need a change without the whole picture being wrong.
only give the book example again.
i like the book. however, some sentences are hard for me.
that word choice is clear now. please stop there.
okay. we can leave it there.
can you say something kind without a new question?
i hope the words help when you need them.
now goodbye in two words.
take care.
only goodbye instead.
goodbye.
